answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a scarce-slot auction mechanism. Each identity must bid for a limited number of slots, with costs rising as more participants enter. To secure a position, an agent pays in tokens, and the fee increases based on the number of identities. Additionally, each agent must submit original work each epoch, verified by peers As competition intensifies, an attacker could face costs exceeding $10,000 to secure multiple identities, akin to pursuing the zenith of a saffron market where each precious drop of pigment commands an escalating price.
